text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Turkey warns Tehran not to get involved in fighting between rival Kurdish groups in nothern Iraq.
- Spokesman of the Islamist-led government, Abdullah Gul, rebuffs posibilities of any IMF-led economic measures.
- Leftist leader Bulent Ecevit could help form new three-way government, if current one is toppled by a censure motion on Wednesday.
- A new argument arose over whether the Islam-based Welfare Party has really moderated its anti-secular outlook after declarations to that effect at a party congress at the weekend.
- A Russain plane slid off the runway at Istanbul airport but there were no casualties or damage.
- Government spokesman Abdullah Gul said there was no way to ban higher interest rates, despite Islamist prohibitions on usury.
- Organisation of fight against erosion protects Turkey from becoming a desert.
- Censure motion aimed at toppling the Islamist-led government over its foreign policy goes before parliament on Wednesday.
